## Discovery & Translational Science

* **CNS-selective plasma p-tau217% accurately captures Alzheimer's pathology and progression** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.05.18.26353208)
  * A preprint study evaluated a next-generation biomarker, brain-derived p-tau217%, which measures the proportion of circulating tau that is CNS-derived and phosphorylated at threonine 217.
  * Across neuropathology and memory clinic cohorts, brain-derived p-tau217% demonstrated higher diagnostic accuracy and better predicted 20-year clinical progression compared to standard plasma p-tau217, p-tau217/Aβ1-42, and non-CNS-selective p-tau217%.
  * Diagnostic performance remained robust in older adults with diabetes and cardiovascular disease, where conventional p-tau217 assays typically suffer from reduced specificity.

* **Evidence mounts for viral vector-associated oncogenesis in gene therapy** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/09/biotech-news-gene-therapy-long-debated-cancer-risk-materializes/)
  * Clinical case reports provide strong evidence that viral vectors used to deliver replacement genes can integrate into host genomes and directly cause tumor formation.
  * The findings validate longstanding theoretical safety concerns regarding insertional mutagenesis in viral vector-mediated gene therapies.

* **International consensus reached on definition of acute-on-chronic liver failure** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/09/acute-on-chronic-liver-failure-new-definition/)
  * Hepatology experts have established a unified diagnostic definition for acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) to standardize patient care and clinical trial recruitment.

* **Carotid body mitochondrial oxygen affinity is impaired in heart failure** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.764874)
  * In an ovine rapid pacing model of heart failure, high-resolution respirometry demonstrated reduced complex IV oxygen affinity in carotid body tissue homogenates.
  * The reduction in mitochondrial oxygen affinity correlated with an elevated hypoxic ventilatory response and increased sympathetic drive, despite no change in net mitochondrial H₂O₂ production or respiration rates.

* **Dynamic magnetic fields suppress psoriasis-like skin lesions via the IL-23/IL-17 axis** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/43000523/)
  * Exposure to a dynamic permanent magnetic field combined with topical calcipotriol significantly reduced skin lesion severity in a mouse model of psoriasis.
  * The anti-inflammatory effect was mediated through downregulation of the IL-23/IL-17 cytokine signaling pathway.

* **Free hemoglobin interferes with bioluminescence assays in renal proximal tubule models** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.764891)
  * Free hemoglobin (fHb) and hemolyzed plasma significantly attenuate bioluminescent signal outputs in human conditionally immortalized proximal tubule epithelial cells (ciPTECs).
  * Removing fHb solutions prior to signal acquisition restored assay baseline; notably, hemolyzed plasma induced minimal NF-κB activation or mitochondrial dysfunction in ciPTECs, challenging assumptions regarding direct fHb cytotoxicity.

* **Reviews highlight advances in KDM targeting and conditional biologics** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41573-026-01561-w)
  * A review summarizes the therapeutic development of small-molecule inhibitors targeting histone lysine demethylases (KDMs) involved in chromatin remodeling and cancer pathogenesis.
  * A companion review details engineering principles for conditional biologics engineered to selectively activate within the tumor microenvironment to expand therapeutic windows in immuno-oncology [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41573-026-01552-x).

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Biotech]** **Janux Therapeutics reports initial Phase 1 data for JANX011** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2119786462443118989)
  * A single 3 mg dose of JANX011 achieved >90% peripheral B-cell depletion in the majority of healthy volunteers in a Phase 1 study.
  * Two trial participants exhibited complete B-cell depletion below the lower limit of quantification.

* **[Biotech]** **Forte Biosciences reports Phase 2 data for PIKTOR in endometrial cancer** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2119768310221086900)
  * Preliminary topline results from the Phase 2 PIK-201 trial evaluating PIKTOR combined with paclitaxel in advanced endometrial cancer demonstrated a confirmed overall response rate (ORR) of 33%.
  * Efficacy-evaluable patients achieved a disease control rate (DCR) of 83%.

* **[Biotech]** **Zura Bio Phase 2 trial of tibulizumab fails primary endpoint in hidradenitis suppurativa** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2119764445501280362)
  * The Phase 2 TibuSHIELD study of tibulizumab (ZB-106) in hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) failed to meet its primary endpoint of percentage change from baseline in total abscess and inflammatory nodule count at Week 16.
  * Key secondary endpoints, including HiSCR50 and HiSCR75, were also missed, leading the company to discontinue tibulizumab development in HS while continuing its Phase 2 TibuSURE trial in systemic sclerosis.

* **Liver-targeted CIDEB siRNA evaluated in adults with MASLD** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMc2612905)
  * *NEJM* published clinical data evaluating an investigational liver-targeted siRNA therapeutic targeting *CIDEB* in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).

* **Dapagliflozin demonstrates renal protection post-heart transplantation** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42999953/)
  * A randomized clinical trial established that SGLT2 inhibition with dapagliflozin provides significant renal protective effects in heart transplant recipients receiving immunosuppressive regimens.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **Eli Lilly GLP-1 pill Foundayo shows efficacy in Phase 3 sleep apnea trials** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/09/eli-lilly-foundayo-sleep-apnea/)
  * Oral GLP-1 candidate Foundayo reduced sleep apnea severity across two late-stage Phase 3 trials.
  * Efficacy efficacy readouts appeared lower than those observed with Lilly’s approved injectable GLP-1/GIP dual agonist Zepbound (tirzepatide).

* **[Big Pharma]** **Phase 3 retatrutide study published for knee osteoarthritis pain and obesity** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2610676)
  * *NEJM* published Phase 3 trial results evaluating once-weekly administration of retatrutide, Eli Lilly's triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist, in adults with obesity and knee osteoarthritis pain.

* **[Biotech]** **Mane reports Phase 3 hair count data for VDPHL01 in androgenetic alopecia** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2119767840266088889)
  * 12-month data from Study 302 evaluating VDPHL01 in male pattern hair loss achieved the highest reported hair count increase across the drug's Phase 3 program to date.

* **Left bundle-branch pacing superior to right ventricular pacing in AV block** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2612972)
  * A randomized trial published in *NEJM* demonstrated improved clinical outcomes with left bundle-branch area pacing compared to conventional right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block.

* **COAST-AF trial evaluates low-voltage area ablation in persistent atrial fibrillation** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42999998/)
  * Topline results from the COAST-AF randomized trial evaluated the efficacy of substrate modification targeting low-voltage areas during catheter ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation.

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **FDA requires NAION safety warnings across GLP-1 receptor agonist class** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-communications/fda-requires-safety-labeling-changes-glucagon-peptide-1-receptor-agonists-glp-1-ras-due-potential)
  * The FDA issued a Drug Safety Communication requiring all GLP-1 receptor agonist manufacturers to add warnings regarding non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) to prescribing information.
  * NAION is a rare condition causing acute, painless loss of vision that can lead to permanent visual impairment.

* **[Biotech]** **FDA accepts sNDA for Celcuity's REVTORPYK in HR+/HER2- breast cancer** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2119785785671188953)
  * The FDA accepted a supplemental NDA for REVTORPYK (gedatolisib) to treat *PIK3CA*-mutated, HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
  * The agency set a PDUFA target action date of June 25, 2027.

* **[Biotech]** **VistaGen completes Type C meeting for Phase 3 fasedienol** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2119786995081982410)
  * VistaGen received regulatory feedback following a Type C meeting with the FDA regarding the Phase 3 clinical development plan for fasedienol nasal spray in social anxiety disorder.

* **FDA actions on opioid use disorder treatments and BsUFA reauthorization** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/food-and-drug-administration-overdose-prevention-framework/medications-opioid-use-disorder)
  * The FDA updated prescribing labeling for transmucosal buprenorphine formulations and launched a national provider campaign to expand access to Medications for Opioid Use Disorder (MOUD).
  * The agency held a public meeting to present recommendations for the Biosimilar User Fee Act (BsUFA) reauthorization covering fiscal years 2028 through 2032 [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/public-meeting-reauthorization-biosimilar-user-fee-act-bsufa-10262026).

## Business & Strategy

* **[Biotech]** **Argenx acquires Unnatural Products macrocyclic peptide platform for $550M upfront** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/argenx-unnatural-products-acquisition-deal-peptides-protein-macrocyclic-immune/874119/)
  * Argenx entered into an agreement to acquire Unnatural Products for $550 million in upfront cash, with additional potential milestone payments.
  * The deal provides Argenx with control over a proprietary macrocyclic peptide technology platform to develop oral immunotherapies for autoimmune conditions.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Novartis discontinues lead cardiovascular candidate** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/11/09/novartis-abandons-heart-drug-bio-fighting-trump-program/)
  * Novartis is abandoning development of a clinical-stage cardiovascular drug following trial data showing no efficacy in preventing myocardial infarction or cardiovascular death.

## Public Health & Policy

* **Federal budget cuts force premature termination of NIH clinical trials** [Science-Based Medicine](https://sciencebasedmedicine.org/devastation-of-nih-funded-clinical-trials-the-price-of-lysenkoism-2-0/)
  * A commentary citing bioethicist Arthur Caplan outlines widespread, premature terminations of NIH-funded clinical trials resulting from administrative budget cuts and mandated research realignment.

* **US issues biosecurity guidelines targeting AI-driven biological risks** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/09/health-news-new-rule-to-prevent-bioweapons/)
  * Federal officials released new biosecurity guidelines aimed at mitigating risks associated with artificial intelligence models capable of designing novel biological agents and potential bioweapons.

* **Advanced responder training fails to improve sudden cardiac arrest survival** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2612757)
  * A major study evaluating community and EMS interventions showed that advanced CPR and defibrillation training for first responders did not yield statistically significant improvements in survival following out-of-hospital sudden cardiac arrest.

* **In vitro modeling identifies anatomical factors driving infant gas rebreathing** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.764821)
  * Aerodynamic modeling of prone infant sleep demonstrated expired gas rebreathing rates >60% even with unobstructed nasal passages.
  * Increasing ambient temperature (23 to 30 °C) increased rebreathing by 68–77%, while increasing nostril diameter (3.2 to 6.0 mm) increased rebreathing by up to 50% due to persistent vortical flow structures near the nasal opening.

**Worth watching:** FDA's class-wide safety warning on GLP-1 receptor agonists and NAION risk may trigger label updates across all marketed obesity and diabetes therapies, potentially impacting clinical monitoring requirements in ongoing trials.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [The BEST Blood Pressure Lowering Exercise Just Got Better!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xF_7CeUimAw) -- Physionic
        - Examines updated literature, including a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, regarding the efficacy of different exercise modalities on 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure in hypertensive adults.
        - Investigates isometric exercise training (IET) and evaluates the dose-response relationship between training frequency and blood pressure control.
        - Details practical protocols and recommendations on how to structure isometric exercise training for optimal blood pressure reduction.
    - [Understanding lab testing: what blood work can & cannot tell you (AMA 91 sneak peek)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HhTirnNCxxE) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Examines the utility and limitations of laboratory testing for assessing lifespan, healthspan, organ systems, and risk across cardiovascular, metabolic, oncologic, and neurodegenerative diseases.
        - Emphasizes the importance of analyzing longitudinal laboratory data over time rather than relying on isolated static measurements.
        - Identifies critical blind spots in blood work where complementary evaluations—such as imaging, body composition analysis, and functional testing—are necessary.
        - Critiques over-testing and direct-to-consumer panels, noting that advanced measures like lipid subfractionation and biological-age scores often lack clinical actionability and fail to reflect physical, cognitive, or emotional health.
    - [s This $15 Billion Valuation Built on Fantasy?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/LA2l1Yw6Lmw) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Features commentary by Sergei Polevikov examining the financial logic behind a $15 billion company valuation.
        - Argues that justifying such a valuation depends on overly optimistic growth assumptions that are not aligned with standard market expectations.
        - Notes that available financial figures and comparable industry metrics fail to support the underlying valuation model.
    - [Who Should Decide What Healthcare AI Can Do?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/4Fg9XfoCxKw) -- Health2Tech
        - Features insights from Alison Curfman regarding governance and oversight in the integration of artificial intelligence into clinical healthcare settings.
        - Emphasizes that practicing clinical experts, rather than outside administrators or developers, must lead AI implementation decisions.
        - Stresses the need to establish explicit clinical standards defining approved use cases as well as boundaries where AI technology should not be applied.
